strings.abandoned.freeze-defect: Abandoned before any prediction: the frozen file was incomplete; a corrected version replaced it.
strings.batch.asteroids.title: Blind asteroid forecasts: how often does the truth land inside our 95% regions?
strings.batch.ephemeris-guided-training: JPL positions told us where to look in the training images (as for Pluto); they never entered the orbit fit or the forecast.
strings.batch.independence: The interval assumes the forecasts are independent. They share one method, one estimate of the two-body model error and SPHEREx's systematic errors, so the true uncertainty is larger than the interval shows.
strings.batch.model-error: A two-body orbit ignores Jupiter's and Saturn's pull. We measured that error on synthetic orbits and added it to every forecast region, so the regions are large.
strings.batch.small-n: A handful of forecasts cannot prove that the 95% regions are calibrated; the interval shows how loosely they constrain it.
strings.batch.team-statement-pending: Counted as prospective only after the team confirms nobody viewed these images.
strings.compare.field-gradient-unknown: How the wavelength changes across the picture is unknown.
strings.compare.field-matched: The wavelengths match across the whole picture.
strings.compare.field-no-matched-pair: No exposure pair with matching wavelengths, so no difference image.
strings.compare.field-shifted: Wavelengths match at the star but not across the whole picture, so no difference image.
strings.compare.matched-pairs: Compared only through exposures with matching wavelengths.
strings.compare.no-exposures: One of the dates has no usable exposure.
strings.compare.no-spectral-overlap: The two pictures saw different wavelengths.
strings.compare.position-different-response: Positions can be compared, but the wavelengths differ.
strings.compare.psf-differs: The star images are sharper on one date than the other (PSF differs by more than 10%), so no difference image.
strings.compare.psf-unknown: The image sharpness (PSF) is not known for one date.
strings.compare.registration-unverified: The sky alignment of these pictures is not confirmed by the pipeline.
strings.compare.response-matched: Same detector and the same wavelength at the star.
strings.compare.response-shifted: Same detector, but the wavelengths differ too much for a brightness comparison.
strings.compare.response-unknown: The wavelength of one picture is unknown.
strings.composite.display-colours: Display colours, not for measurement: red = arrays 5-6, green = 3-4, blue = 1-2.
strings.composite.missing-array-group: No colour picture for this date: one of the three array groups has no pictures.
strings.context.allwise-w2: AllWISE W2 (4.6 µm) single exposures, with their dates
strings.context.no-source-on-track: Not detected: no source within 3 arcsec of where the target was on that date.
strings.context.not-like-for-like: Other telescopes use other filters: compare positions and dates, not brightness.
strings.context.service-failed: The catalogue service could not be reached when this file was made.
strings.context.twomass-ks: 2MASS Ks (2.2 µm), with its own observation date

strings.exclude.contaminated: Positions spoiled by a catalogued neighbour are not used.
strings.exclude.fewer-than-3: Fewer than 3 identified exposures means insufficient data.
strings.exclude.identification: Positions not identified as the target are not used.
strings.exclude.not-measured: No position could be measured in this exposure.
strings.exclude.quality-gate: Exposures that fail the SPHEREx quality check are not used.
strings.explain.brightness-insufficient: No pair of dates has the same wavelength and clean pixels at the star ({n_flagged} of {n_exposures} pictures have saturated or flagged pixels on it), so no brightness change is reported.
strings.explain.brightness-measured: In matching wavelengths the star was {value} times as bright on date B as on date A (± {sigma}).
strings.explain.control: Check: {n_stars} ordinary field stars were measured the same way and compared with Gaia. Share that agree within the 95% region: {fraction}.
strings.explain.fixed-sky-pair: Two dates of the same patch of sky: the body moves across the background stars.
strings.explain.motion-contaminated: The target's light overlaps a catalogued neighbour star (G {neighbour_g_mag}, about {neighbour_arcsec} arcsec away) in {n_contaminated} pictures, so no motion is reported.
strings.explain.motion-insufficient: The SPHEREx exposures here do not give enough clean positions to measure the motion.
strings.explain.motion-measured: SPHEREx positions from {n_points} exposures over {days} days give a proper motion of {value} ± {sigma} arcsec per year. Gaia DR3 lists {catalogue} arcsec per year.
strings.explain.moving-object-cutouts: Each picture is centred on where the ephemeris puts the body at that moment, so the stars move and the body stays near the centre.
strings.explain.not-available: SPHEREx data for this target are not available here yet: {reason}.
strings.explain.see-only: This target is shown for looking only. It is not part of the prediction tests.
strings.explain.training-only: Only the training visits are opened. The newest visit stays closed until the prediction is frozen.
strings.forecast.after-2026-miss: Made after the 2026 miss, using its lessons; check when IRSA releases the data.
strings.hindcast.v2-label: Exploratory, after the reveal: the new method tried on the 2026 visit. It does not count.
strings.holdout.newest-visit: The newest visit is held out for checking.
strings.holdout.newest-visit-window: The newest visit is held out for checking.
strings.holdout.next-visit-forecast: Open forecast for the next visit, not yet released.
strings.ident.catalogue-gate: The star must lie within 3 arcsec of its catalogue track with no other catalogued star nearby.
strings.ident.frozen-model-search: Search around the frozen forecast; a source must also be absent there on another date of the visit.
strings.lesson.brightness.formula: magnitude change = -2.5 x log10(ratio); z = (ratio - 1) / sigma
strings.lesson.brightness.q1: Another pair of dates gives a ratio of {ratio} ± {sigma}. Convert it to magnitudes. Is |z| below 1.96 (no clear change)?
strings.lesson.brightness.q2: Barnard's Star had flagged (saturated) pixels on it in {n_flagged} of {n_exposures} SPHEREx pictures. What fraction is that, and why does it stop a brightness measurement?
strings.lesson.brightness.teacher: Only pictures taken at the same wavelength can be compared, and a star too bright for the detector cannot be measured at all. Saying 'we cannot tell' is a correct scientific answer.
strings.lesson.brightness.title: Did it get brighter? Comparing like with like
strings.lesson.brightness.worked: On two dates, at the same wavelength, Epsilon Indi B's brightness ratio was {ratio} ± {sigma}. What is the change in magnitudes, and is it larger than the uncertainty?
strings.lesson.distance.formula: angle between two sky positions; light time = distance x 8.32 minutes per au; distance (pc) = 1 / parallax (arcsec)
strings.lesson.distance.q1: Pluto appeared to move {separation_deg}° in {days} days. What was its average apparent speed in degrees per day?
strings.lesson.distance.q2: Our orbit fit puts Pluto {distance_au} au from the Sun. Light crosses 1 au in {au_light_minutes} minutes. How many hours does sunlight take to reach Pluto?
strings.lesson.distance.q3: Gaia measures Barnard's Star's parallax as {parallax_arcsec} arcsec. How far away is it in parsecs?
strings.lesson.distance.teacher: Pluto's apparent motion is mostly Earth's own motion seen against a distant object; that is why an orbit fit needs the observer's position. The distance comes from our own fit to two SPHEREx visits (modelled, not measured directly).
strings.lesson.distance.title: How far away? Motion and distance
strings.lesson.distance.worked: SPHEREx saw Pluto at RA {visit1_ra_deg}°, Dec {visit1_dec_deg}° (MJD {visit1_mjd}) and at RA {visit2_ra_deg}°, Dec {visit2_dec_deg}° (MJD {visit2_mjd}). How far apart on the sky are these two positions?
strings.lesson.how-sure.formula: hit if D² ≤ 5.991 (95% region in 2D); expected hits = 0.95 × N; chance all hit = 0.95^N (only if independent)
strings.lesson.how-sure.q1: If {n_trials} independent forecasts each have a true 95% region, how many hits do you expect?
strings.lesson.how-sure.q2: What is the chance that all {n_trials} hit?
strings.lesson.how-sure.q3: We scored {n_hits} hits out of {n_trials}. What fraction is that? Can 3 trials prove the regions are right?
strings.lesson.how-sure.teacher: Two of our three checked forecasts were retrospective (the data had been seen) and catalogue-assisted; the only prospective one (Pluto) missed narrowly. A handful of trials cannot prove a 95% calibration; misses are reported, not hidden.
strings.lesson.how-sure.title: How sure are we? Checking forecasts honestly
strings.lesson.how-sure.worked: Our frozen Pluto forecast scored D² = {d2}. The 95% threshold is {threshold}. Hit or miss?
strings.limit.aperture-whole-pixels: Brightness is summed over whole pixels inside a circle.
strings.limit.blended-binary: This is a close pair of stars; at SPHEREx resolution both are measured together.
strings.limit.catalogue-assisted-identification: The star was found using its catalogue position and motion.
strings.limit.control-not-passed: The field-star check did not pass, so the uncertainty may be underestimated.
strings.limit.detection-not-validated: No detection of this body has been validated in these pictures.
strings.limit.differential-photometry: Brightness ratios are divided by the median ratio of ordinary field stars on the same dates.
strings.limit.ephemeris-guided: Cutouts follow the JPL Horizons ephemeris (catalogue-assisted).
strings.limit.ephemeris-guided-training: Training cutouts were centred with the JPL ephemeris; the forecast itself does not use it.
strings.limit.few-visits-parallax: Only a few visits: the parallax fit is sensitive to small errors that differ from visit to visit.
strings.limit.gaussian-psf-model: Positions come from a simple bell-shaped star model, not the full SPHEREx PSF.
strings.limit.identification-gate: A position counts only within 3 arcsec of the catalogue track and with no other catalogued source within 12 arcsec.
strings.limit.joint-fit-epochs: The body is too faint for single pictures; each date's position comes from one fit to all its pictures together.
strings.limit.no-parallax-baseline: Straight-line fit that ignores parallax: a simple comparison, not the best model.
strings.limit.official-table-positions: Pictures are centred on the comet positions given in the official SPHEREx exposure table.
strings.limit.parallax-from-catalogue: The yearly parallax wobble uses the Gaia distance (catalogue-assisted).
strings.limit.parallax-not-modelled: The yearly parallax wobble is not modelled.
strings.limit.photometric-floor: Brightness errors include the scatter seen between pictures taken on the same date.
strings.limit.saturated-core-wing-fit: The star's centre is saturated; its position comes from the outer glow only.
strings.limit.see-only: For looking only: no measurement or prediction is made for this target.
strings.limit.single-group-latest-visit: The newest visit has only one detector group, so the forecast leans on few pictures.
strings.limit.two-body-only: Orbit model: Sun only (planets' pulls neglected over this short arc).
strings.limit.visit-systematics: The free parallax fit disagrees with Gaia, a sign of visit-to-visit errors; uncertainties may be too small.
strings.limit.wcs-wave-approximate: Wavelengths come from the approximate lookup table in each file (about 1 nm).
strings.measure.annulus-too-small: Too few clean sky pixels around the star.
strings.measure.aperture-empty: No pixels inside the measuring circle.
strings.measure.baseline-too-short: The dates span too short a time for a motion fit.
strings.measure.contaminated: Another catalogued source lies within 12 arcsec and could spoil this measurement.
strings.measure.fit-at-bound: The star model hit a limit; the position is not trusted.
strings.measure.fit-failed: The star model did not fit.
strings.measure.fit-singular: The star model could not be constrained.
strings.measure.flagged-pixels-in-aperture: Flagged pixels (for example saturation) cover the star.
strings.measure.low-snr: The star is too faint here for a reliable position.
strings.measure.no-measured-matched-pair: No matching-wavelength pair with clean pixels at the star.
strings.measure.no-photometric-control: Too few comparison stars with matching wavelengths on both dates to check the brightness scale.
strings.measure.not-target: The fitted source is more than 3 arcsec from where the catalogue puts the target, so it is not counted.
strings.measure.null-test-failed: A check with shuffled times also found a signal (likely a star), so this is not counted.
strings.measure.outside-cutout: The star is outside this picture.
strings.measure.repeatability-unknown: Too few same-date picture pairs to check how repeatable the brightness is.
strings.measure.too-few-epochs: Too few positions for a motion fit.
strings.measure.too-few-good-pixels: Too few clean pixels around the star.
strings.planetx.fields-note: Measured on fields we had already opened: the five challenge-target fields and the training visits of Pluto and Makemake. Never on the reserved 3I/ATLAS path.
strings.planetx.game.label: Artificial planet added for this game
strings.planetx.game.rule: Two real SPHEREx exposures of the same field, taken days apart. We added one faint artificial source that moves as a body 500 AU away would. Can you find it?
strings.planetx.limit.few-exposures: Six exposures per field and band: per-field curves have wide intervals; the pooled curve is the main result.
strings.planetx.limit.gaussian-detector: Detection uses the site's own Gaussian fit, which is less sensitive than an optimal fit with the true PSF.
strings.planetx.limit.model-dependent: Planet Nine's brightness depends on its unknown mass, distance, albedo and atmosphere. Broad-band magnitudes are compared with narrow SPHEREx channels as if the spectrum were flat across the band. Methane absorbs strongly near 3.3 µm, so for a methane-bearing atmosphere our 3.25–3.55 µm channels would see less than the W1 average and the gap would grow; a channel inside a methane window would see more and the gap would shrink.
strings.planetx.limit.single-exposure: These depths are for single exposures in one spectral channel, not for the full mission.
strings.planetx.limit.variance-unchanged: The artificial source's own photon noise was not added; at these faint levels the zodiacal background dominates.
strings.planetx.mission-sensitivity: SPHEREx's published sensitivities are per spectral channel after all four all-sky surveys (pre-launch estimates). One exposure is shallower; the Sky Simulator paper gives pre-launch single-visit values.
strings.planetx.motion-note: Seen from Earth, a body 300–1000 AU away shifts by tens to hundreds of arcseconds within one SPHEREx visit and by many arcminutes between visits, so its light never piles up in one place. A real search has to shift and stack the exposures along trial paths.
strings.planetx.note.f16: Fortney et al. (2016): cloud-free atmospheres at 622 AU with Neptune's radius; methane depletion moves flux into the 3–5 µm window.
strings.planetx.note.fortney-system: Fortney et al. do not name the magnitude system. They compare their W1 values with WISE's Vega limits, so we read them as Vega.
strings.planetx.note.lm16: Linder & Mordasini (2016): blackbody spectrum, 10 Earth masses, Vega-based magnitudes. Perihelion and aphelion values use the paper's own rule (reflected light scales as 1/r⁴: 4 mag brighter at 280 AU, 2 mag fainter at 1120 AU).
strings.planetx.note.meisner-system: Meisner et al. do not name the system; WISE catalogue magnitudes are Vega (WISE Explanatory Supplement IV.4.h).
strings.planetx.note.single-visit: Pre-launch Sky Simulator estimate for one visit in one spectral channel (112.5 s), limited by zodiacal light.
strings.planetx.note.wise-limit: Meisner et al. (2018) found no Planet Nine brighter than W1 = 16.7 (Vega, 90% complete) over most of the high-latitude sky, using WISE and NEOWISE images stacked along trial orbits.
strings.planetx.optimal-note: Reference, not a recovery measurement: the magnitude at which an optimal fit with the true ePSF would reach S/N 5, computed from each exposure's VARIANCE at clean positions (range over exposures). The site's Gaussian detector reaches 50% about 1 magnitude brighter.
strings.planetx.projection-assumptions: Assumes background-limited noise, perfect motion compensation, no confusion with other sources and exposures of equal depth in the same channel.
strings.planetx.projection-note: Projection, not a measurement: the depth if N exposures were stacked along the planet's true path and the noise fell as 1/√N.
strings.planetx.psf-test: PSF check: on bright isolated stars, the ePSF zone nearest the star fits better than the zone a swapped x/y reading would pick.
strings.planetx.realism-note: Check on real stars: the site's fit finds real isolated stars about as often as injected sources of the same measured brightness where both are bright. At the faint end real stars are found less often, as expected when noise scatters faint stars to brighter measured values.
strings.planetx.rule.found: Found means the site's own fit measures a source at S/N of at least 5 within 1 pixel (6.15″) of where the artificial source was added.
strings.planetx.scenario.f16-50k-methane-poor: Fortney et al. 2016, 50 K, methane-poor (10⁻⁶), their brightest case
strings.planetx.scenario.lm16-aphelion: Linder & Mordasini 2016, 10 Earth masses at aphelion (1120 AU)
strings.planetx.scenario.lm16-nominal: Linder & Mordasini 2016, 10 Earth masses at 700 AU
strings.planetx.scenario.lm16-perihelion: Linder & Mordasini 2016, 10 Earth masses at perihelion (280 AU)
strings.planetx.title: Could SPHEREx see Planet X? We measured it.
strings.planetx.verdict.summary: One SPHEREx exposure finds half of the artificial sources at AB {depth_i} near 0.8 µm, AB {depth_w1} near 3.4 µm and AB {depth_w2} near 4.6 µm. The nominal Planet Nine of Linder & Mordasini (2016) would be AB {model_i}, {model_w1} and {model_w2}: {gap_w1} magnitudes too faint at 3.4 µm. Only the brightest published scenarios come within reach, and the planet moves too far between exposures to pile up its light without a shift-and-stack search.
strings.planetx.verdict.too-faint: Too faint for one exposure: the prediction is fainter than the magnitude at which one SPHEREx exposure finds half of the artificial sources (gap = prediction minus our 50% depth, positive).
strings.planetx.verdict.within-depth: Within reach of one exposure: the prediction is brighter than the magnitude at which one SPHEREx exposure finds half of the artificial sources (gap = prediction minus our 50% depth, negative).
strings.predict.fewer-than-2-visits: Fewer than two training visits kept enough detections, so no orbit was fitted.
strings.predict.fit-failed: The model could not be fitted to the training data.
strings.predict.no-period-model: No period model justified by the training data.
strings.predict.no-training-measurements: No usable training brightness measurements: no prediction can be made.
strings.predict.no-training-positions: No usable training positions: no prediction can be made.
strings.predict.orbit-unconstrained: The training positions do not constrain an orbit.
strings.predict.too-few-training-positions: Too few training positions (or only one visit) for a defensible prediction.
strings.product.unusable-quality-metadata: The file's quality flags could not be read safely.
strings.quality.l2-dqa-not-pass: The SPHEREx quality check did not pass for this exposure.
strings.quality.target-outside-cutout: The target is outside this exposure's picture.
strings.quantity.control_fraction_within_95pct: Field-star check: share of comparison stars whose measured motion agrees with Gaia
strings.quantity.flux_ratio_b_over_a: Brightness ratio, date B over date A, same wavelength
strings.quantity.parallax_arcsec: Parallax from SPHEREx positions alone (arcsec, exploratory)
strings.quantity.proper_motion_east_arcsec_yr: Proper motion towards east (arcsec per year)
strings.quantity.proper_motion_north_arcsec_yr: Proper motion towards north (arcsec per year)
strings.quantity.proper_motion_total_linear_arcs: Total proper motion, straight-line fit without parallax (arcsec per year)
strings.reserved.released-nothing-to-verify: Released: the trial was frozen as insufficient data, so nothing is left to protect.
strings.reserved.released-verified: Released: the frozen forecast has been checked against these data.
strings.reserved.rule: Live loading is paused near these paths so reserved observations stay unopened.
strings.reserved.see-only: See-only target: live loading is paused along its path.
strings.reserved.until-predictions-frozen: Until the predictions are frozen and published.
strings.reserved.until-verified: The prediction is frozen; the data stay closed until the pre-registered check opens them.
strings.train.blended-gaia: A catalogued star lies within 12″: the position could be blended, not used.
strings.train.download-failed: The cutout could not be downloaded.
strings.train.l2-quality: Exposure failed SPHEREx's own quality check.
strings.train.off-track: Fitted source more than 3″ from where the object should be: not used.
strings.unavailable.holdout-closed: the newest visit is reserved for the prediction test
strings.unavailable.no-current-product: the exposure listed in the official table has no current (DR1) product
strings.verify.fewer-than-3: Fewer than 3 exposures could be identified, so the check is not possible.
strings.verify.motion-inconsistent: The candidate positions do not move together with the forecast: ambiguous.
strings.verify.multiple-candidates: More than one source passed the identification rules: ambiguous.
strings.verify.singular-covariance: The uncertainties could not be combined (singular covariance).
